Blocking findings (documentation accuracy / known-gap integrity; no code fix is required in this docs PR, but the model must disclose them or code tasks must land):
1. [High] Secret env inheritance is claimed impossible but is not prevented. SECURITY-MODEL.md:111,155-158,258-260 and README.md:260-261 say allowlisted provider keys are never inherited by child processes; lua/wheel/host.lua:210-223 runs `io.popen(shell_string)` with the parent environment, and `run_command` (tool.lua:613-650) uses it with no scrubbing. Every child sees OPENAI_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. Known gaps 685-687 omit this.
2. [High] File-tool shell interpolation bypasses the path sandbox and deny-list. tool.lua:665-676 (list_directory -> host.lua:141-144 `ls -la %q`), tool.lua:712-730 (search_code -> `grep ... %q %q`), and tool.lua:638 (cwd) interpolate model-controlled values with Lua `%q`, not argv/shell_quote; `$()` in a path executes (reproduced harmlessly in /tmp). SECURITY-MODEL.md:337-366 says every command string is screened; known gaps omit this.
3. [High] Trust/state paths are not excluded from workspace authority. SECURITY-MODEL.md:131-133 says tools cannot read/write the trust store/audit/global config even under $HOME; tool.lua:91-178 only enforces root containment, and config.lua:380-428 writes $XDG_STATE_HOME/wheel/trusted_projects.json. A home-rooted workspace lets write_file self-approve a malicious .wheel/init.lua (defeating D5). Known gaps 680-690 mention the non-XDG fallback but not this bypass.
4. [High] `.git` is model-writable. SECURITY-MODEL.md:134-137 says direct rewrites of Git internals are not a tool primitive, but write_file (tool.lua:481-508) can write `.git/hooks/*` or `.git/config`, giving code execution at the next Git command; no guard and no known-gap entry.
5. [Medium-High] Deny-list coverage is overstated. SECURITY-MODEL.md:337-355 lists 10 categories; tool.lua:184-199 implements about 5 and has no sudo/su/doas/pkexec, setuid/setgid, credential-store exfiltration, remote-pipe, audit/trust tampering, ownership-outside-root, or detach screening. SECURITY-MODEL.md:673-674 calls it "categorical"; the only related known gap (695-696) concerns error shape.
6. [Medium] Atomic-write claim contradicts the model and code. README.md:163 says write_file is "atomic"; README.md:159 and SECURITY-MODEL.md:682-683 say atomic writes are not implemented; tool.lua:503 truncates with `io.open("w")`.
7. [Medium] "WheelHost concentrates filesystem ... calls" is false. SECURITY-MODEL.md:677-678 and CHANGELOG.md:44-47 claim filesystem operations route through the seam, but tool.lua:411,489,503,542,582 and config.lua:316-336 use `io.open` directly; host.lua:9-12 itself scopes direct `io.open` out.
8. [Medium] Role matrix is not enforced. SECURITY-MODEL.md:314-321 says Commander "Custom mutating" = Deny and lists Primary; tool.lua:237-241 only denies Commander Modify, and agent.lua:31-37 has no Primary role. Known gaps 695-696 do not disclose.
9. [Low] Instruction-budget wording is inaccurate. SECURITY-MODEL.md:698-699 says there is no instruction budget, but config.lua:562-568 installs a 100000-instruction count hook (tests/test_wheel.lua:1316-1320 assert it). The hook is catchable through the exposed pcall (config.lua:541-542; reproduced with a pcall loop), so the precise gap is "catchable instruction hook; no wall-clock or memory budget."
10. [Low] Other unimplemented policy bullets are missing from known gaps: NUL/control rejection (SECURITY-MODEL.md:299 vs tool.lua:91-178), stdin/TTY off and detached/sudo/setuid denial (164-170 vs host.lua:210-223), no implicit CI trust (397-398 vs config.lua:650-651,680-687), multi-root operation (141-143 vs a single env.workspace_root), and the OQ-068 attribution "no consumer executes a project entry" (469-472; OQ-068 at bitty-docs/docs/decisions/open-questions.md:75 says declarative-data-only).

Design: Option A (retained leader), chosen over /proc session/start-time verification (B) because it is deterministic, portable, and removes the reuse window instead of narrowing it with platform-specific identity heuristics. The `setsid -w` session leader records $$ (its PID = PGID) in the exclusive 0600 pgid file, runs the command under `timeout --foreground` (so expiry signals only the direct child and the leader survives to record status), waits for the command, writes the direct exit status to the private status file BEFORE any signal, ignores TERM, sends TERM to -$$, sleeps the 250 ms grace, writes the `swept` marker, then KILLs -$$ as the last identity-holding action. While the leader is alive the PGID cannot be allocated to another process, so the sweep can only target the recorded group; the normal, timeout, and TERM-ignoring paths have no PID/PGID reuse window. If the leader dies before the sweep (external SIGKILL/OOM), no signal is sent: a missing status is a typed failure with cleanup=unverified and a message that the group was not swept; a present status without the sweep marker is cleanup=unverified with a stderr note.

Result shape adds `cleanup` (swept|unverified|not_run) and `pgid`. The pgid file is a recorded artifact, not the signal selector. command_runner doubles report cleanup=not_run. No pkill/killall/pgrep/name-pattern anywhere; only kill -TERM/-KILL -$$. No manifest, command-catalog, authority, or dependency widening; 14 commands and the lazy/eager split are unchanged (the fixture asserts 14/14).

NEEDS-FIX independent review of frozen commit 1db5196 against origin/main (762a82d). Findings:
1. Handoff acceptance is not a durable atomic state transition. lua/wheel/team.lua:681-695 reassigns the kernel task (advancing generation) before persisting the accepted record. If persistence fails, compensation reassigns again and updates only the in-memory record; the compensating _persist_handoff result is ignored. A second failure leaves the durable offered record at the old generation while task ownership/generation has changed. Also _persist_handoff at :564-583 rolls the slot back after checkpoint creation fails, but cannot roll back the already-created immutable context commit/reflog, so failure does not restore prior context state. Add injected failures at each stage and prove recoverable consistent state or redesign as atomic/fenced transition.
2. Acting identity/session authority is not enforced for state transitions. set_handoff_state(handoff_id,target_state) at :656-679 has no caller/target identity parameter and accepts/rejects/closes solely by ID; any team consumer can accept another agent's offer or close an accepted handoff. Session references are optional and validated only if supplied at :443-459; when supplied, state=created/paused is accepted and there is no controller attachment/authority or target-session match at acceptance. Require the target agent and authorized live controller session to accept, and an authorized owner to reject/close.
3. Task completion/release is not fully generation-fenced. release_task at :386-395 treats an already-succeeded task as success without checking current task generation/worker ownership; a stale local claim can then increment completion and clear assignment. Validate current task generation and worker before all terminal cleanup, including already-terminal idempotent paths.
4. Handoff persistence is overstated/ambiguous. README.md:80-84 says handoffs are not a durable cross-process store, while CHANGELOG says records are stored in the existing context slot and CTX-0047 requires durable handoffs. Context slots/checkpoints here are WheelContext in-memory projections; _find_handoff can only recover when another caller supplies the same/reconstructed Context, and it restores task ownership but not durable agent/session state. Define the durability boundary and provide a real supported restart/cross-process recovery test, or explicitly narrow the feature claim. ContextRef is only a bounded arbitrary text field, not validated/resolved against Runner ContextRef records.
5. Parent-task metadata validation is incomplete against normalized task APIs: create_task only validates parent_task_id syntax/existence/self-parent and copies dependency list without checking parent field interactions, and lifecycle_status is added only to the mock dispatcher; confirm production bridge contract/serialization and normalized status availability outside mock mode. Parent hierarchy is otherwise kept separate from dependencies.
